newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks seen ranged at end of correction.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks seen ranged at end of correction.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks are seen opening ranged on Tuesday as investors wait out a market correction that began last week, brokers said.
"Activity should be dull due to mopping up by sellers who have been taking profit and as buyers keep low to see if the market has corrected," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
Colombo stocks, which rose over 15 percent in March and April on improved investor sentiment, began a correction on April 23.
The all share index closed up on Monday, the first time in three days, rising 1.7 points to 717.9 on a turnover of 105.8 million rupees.
"Barring an exceptional transaction involving a pricey blue chip, the market should be pretty dull," said a broker who declined to be identified.
Final turnover is expected to be supported by a parcel of 3.8 million shares of Agalawatte Plantations at 32 rupees each, which was expected to be concluded on Tuesday.
The shares were put on bid on Friday on an all-or-none basis for three days as required by the Stock Exchange when five percent or more of a company's issued capital is up for sale.
